findings: 2026-11-05: drafted for Mathematics 11 Unit 8 (owner request): English and a teacher-style Roman Urdu lesson; the book's content in order with our clearly labelled teaching notes; worked examples step by step with reasons; results verified with sympy.

Book correction: Example 28: the book prints "\text{Cost} = C \times (1 + x)^{n} = 100 \times (1 + 0.05)^{3}"; the base cost is C = \text{Rs. } 100{,}000. It then prints 100{,}000 \times 1.1575 = 1157500 and "Rs. 1,157,500". Correct: 100{,}000 \times 1.1575 = 115{,}750, so the total cost is about Rs. 115,750.

Book correction: Example 29: the book's Induction of Hypothesis reads "if the first k dominoes fall, then the kth domino will also fall". What has to be shown is that the (k + 1)-th domino falls; the next paragraph of the book says this correctly.

Book correction: Example 30: the book prints A = 100{,}000 \times (1 + 0.05)^{1 \times 3} = 1000 \times (1.05)^{3}; the factor stays 100,000. It also prints "1 + 0.15 + 0.0075 - 0.000125"; the last term is +0.000125. Both totals in the book (1.157625 and Rs. 115,762.5) are right.

Book correction: Example 31: the book's formula I_{n} = 250 + 250 \times (0.4)^{n} is wrong: it gives I_{1} = 350, while the recurrence gives I_{1} = 0.4(500) + 100 = 300. The book's inductive step reaches 200 + 100(0.4)^{k} and then rewrites it as 250 - 50 + 100(0.4)^{k+1}, which is a different number, so nothing is proved.
